I1.quote: Searched main text, Table 1, Figs. 1-5 and SI (Figs. S1-S2) for a gravimetric, volumetric or flow measurement of gas-phase H2 uptake by any sorbent; none found. H2 appears only as a reactant in CO/CO2 hydrogenation (conversion, STY), and H2 storage on CNTs is only cited from ref. [12].

I5.quote: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube (CNT) arrays were dispersed in Na2CO3 solution and co-precipitated with metal nitrite to form long CNTs (over 500 μm) intercrossed Cu/Zn/Al/Zr catalyst (CD703).

notes: Catalysis paper on methanol/DME synthesis over a CNT (15 wt%)-Cu/Zn/Al/Zr catalyst; reported quantities are CO/CO2 conversion and space time yield (Table 1, Figs. 3-5). The only hydrogen-storage statement is quoted from other work: 'As reported by Dong et al., ... CNTs can reversibly adsorb and store a considerably greater amount of hydrogen [12]' (main, p. 4, Section 3.5). Not a review, not retracted, no duplicate-data statement, so the I1 failure is coded no_conditions_stated (not theoretical, not electrochemical).
